summary: Planned commercial block on the Potrero Power Station masterplan (the design guidelines permit office and laboratory/life-science uses), paired with Block 11 in the project engineer's description of about 430,000 sq ft of office with below-grade parking (the Planning Department's October 2020 Phase 1 approval lists about 177,000 sq ft of commercial space for Block 12 and 219,000 for Block 11, about 396,000 together; the sources differ and are not reconciled). Design was under review as of the March 2025 annual compliance report. In a request reported July 29, 2026, the developer asked to raise Block 12's height by 23 feet and let it become residential or commercial; the Planning Commission approved the amendment unanimously (reported Aug 3, 2026) and the Board of Supervisors passed the amended development agreement on first reading on Sept 29, 2026, and Legistar lists it enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Mayor 'APPROVED'); the enacted height map gives Block 12 123 ft, or 115 ft if majority non-residential (100 ft in the adopted rules), taking effect Nov 13, 2026 by our count. No construction start found.

milestones.text: Blocks 11, 12 and 15 covered together at a community pre-application meeting for design review

Planning Department approves the Phase 1 Development Phase Application, which includes Block 12 (Development Phase Approval dated October 7, 2020, Case No. 2017-011878PHA, signed by Planning Director Rich Hillis): the approval lists 'Block 12 – Includes construction of approximately 177,000 square feet of commercial, 6,000 square feet of PDR, 25,000 square feet of entertainment, arts and recreation, and 27,000 square feet of accessory parking uses' (PDF p. 16), says the first phase consists of 'vertical improvements to Blocks 2, 7, 8, 11, 12, and 15' (PDF p. 2), and its Decision reads 'approves the Phase 1 Plan Application dated October 6, 2020' (PDF p. 4). The approval moves 'the construction of commercial buildings on Blocks 11, 12, and 15' into Development Phase 1 (PDF p. 3). The date is the approval's own date, an event date. This approves the development phase, not Block 12's building design; no design review approval has been found for the block.

'Blocks 11 and 12 Design Review Application' dated February 2021 (the 2024 annual compliance report gives both February 24, 2021 and February 4, 2021); the report cites it for the Block 11 childcare space and the La Cocina PDR space designed into Blocks 11 and 12
2024 annual compliance report states designs for Blocks 11 and 12 'are under review' (i.e., not yet approved) as of report submission

Developer proposes a Development Agreement amendment increasing Block 12's permitted height by 23 feet, and giving Block 12 flexibility to become residential instead of commercial; the Chronicle's July 29, 2026 article says the Planning Commission considered the request 'On Thursday' (the hearing date is not stated there), and the commission approved the amendment unanimously, sending it to the Board of Supervisors (SF Standard, August 3, 2026); the Board of Supervisors then passed the amendment package on first reading on Sept 29, 2026 (next entry)

Board of Supervisors passes the Amended and Restated Development Agreement (BOS File 260724) and the Planning Code and Zoning Map ordinance for the Potrero Power Station Special Use District (BOS File 260770) on first reading; Legistar's history lists '9/29/2026 ... Board of Supervisors ... PASSED, ON FIRST READING ... Pass' for both. Final passage on October 6, 2026 and the Mayor's approval and enactment on October 13, 2026 are the next entries on this timeline. All dates here are legislative event dates as listed by the Clerk of the Board (first-reading row read October 12 and again October 14, 2026)

Board of Supervisors finally passes the Amended and Restated Development Agreement ordinance (BOS File 260724) and the Planning Code and Zoning Map ordinance for the Potrero Power Station Special Use District (BOS File 260770): the Clerk of the Board's 'Leg Final' attachment to each file lists 'October 06, 2026 Board of Supervisors - FINALLY PASSED', 'Ayes: 11 - Chan, Chen, Dorsey, Fielder, Mahmood, Mandelman, Melgar, Sauter, Sherrill, Walton and Wong' (File 260724 attachment pp. 11-12; File 260770 attachment pp. 58-59), and the Clerk's certificate says each ordinance 'was FINALLY PASSED on 10/6/2026 by the Board of Supervisors'. The date is the Board's vote date, an event date. The Legistar history row for 10/6/2026 on each file's web page carries no action text, so the attachment is the source for this entry. The Mayor's approval and enactment followed on October 13, 2026 (next entry).

Mayor approves the Amended and Restated Development Agreement (BOS File 260724) and the Planning Code and Zoning Map ordinance for the Potrero Power Station Special Use District (BOS File 260770): Legistar lists both as 'Status: Passed' with 'Final action: 10/13/2026', 'Enactment date: 10/13/2026' and enactment numbers 208-26 (File 260724) and 209-26 (File 260770), and a history row '10/13/2026 ... Mayor ... APPROVED' for each. The Board's final passage on October 6, 2026 (11 ayes) is the previous entry on this timeline. October 13, 2026 is the enactment date, from the Clerk of the Board's listing (page read October 14 and again October 17, 2026); it is an event date. Both ordinances provide 'This ordinance shall become effective on the 31st day after enactment' (File 260770 §5(a), p. 56 of its 'Leg Final' attachment; File 260724, p. 10 of its attachment); counted from October 13, 2026 that is November 13, 2026, a legal date computed by Pier & Point and not printed in the text.

Completion expected: Block 12 is part of Phase 1 (per the 2024 annual compliance report's Phase 1 list, Blocks 2, 7, 8, 11, 12, 15), whose development schedule runs 2020-2029 under the October 2020 Phase 1 approval; SocketSite's block-by-block table for that program shows Block 12 vertical development 2027-2029
milestones.basis_note: Phase 1 in the October 7, 2020 Phase 1 and Phasing Plan Amendment approval (section 2.7, 'Phase 1 Development Schedule: Years 2020 - 2029', expected to take 10 years); SocketSite (Oct 9, 2020) block table gives Block 12 vertical development 2027-2029 (its text also says the first phase would be completed in 2028). A 2020 forecast, not a Block 12 commitment -- design for Blocks 11/12 was still 'under review' (not approved) as of the March 2025 compliance report, and the Board of Supervisors passed an Amended and Restated Development Agreement including Phasing Plan amendments (BOS File 260724) on first reading on Sept 29, 2026 and finally on Oct 6, 2026, and Legistar lists it enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Enactment No. 208-26); its timing for Block 12 has not been read here.

milestones.text: Board of Supervisors approves the Potrero Power Station project and Development Agreement (Ordinance No. 62-20, Board File 200040), the entitlement covering the adopted Design for Development, whose Land Use Table (Table 3.1.1) lists Block 12 (the Planning Commission had voted 5-0 on January 30, 2020 to recommend approval of the project); the Development Agreement's own effective date is May 25, 2020, distinct from the D4D's own February 26, 2020 final-document date. (Block 12 was later named one of Phase 1's six blocks by the October 2020 Phase 1 Development Phase Application -- a construction-phase assignment, not when it first entered the plan.)

details.text: Permitted uses on Block 12: the adopted D4D final Table 3.1.1 permits Non-Retail Sales/Services (office) and Laboratory/Life Science uses, with Residential Not Permitted. The Sept 28, 2026 committee version of the amendment package (passed on first reading Sept 29, 2026; enacted Oct 13, 2026 per Legistar, final text not yet checked against this record) would permit residential use on Block 12: the revised legislative digest says 'the ordinance would allow residential uses on Block 12'.

2026 height amendment for Block 12: the enacted height map (BOS File 260770 'Leg Final' attachment, p. 29, Figure 249.87-2) labels Block 12 "123'", and its Note 2 reads "Maximum height limit on Block 12 shall be limited to 115' if the building is majority non-Residential Use." The Sept 28, 2026 draft Design for Development labelled Block 12 "123' Residential Maximum Building Height" and "115' Commercial Maximum Building Height" (Appendix A.11); the adopted D4D's Appendix A.11 labels it "100' Maximum". The map is read from the rendered page (Leg Final, p. 29, Figure 249.87-2 'Building Heights Maximum'; its legend reads 'Maximum Height/ Maximum Base Height'); the PDF's text layer for the map is unreliable, so the labels were read by eye. The Board finally passed the ordinance on Oct 6, 2026 and Legistar lists it enacted on Oct 13, 2026. The ordinance takes effect on the 31st day after enactment ('This ordinance shall become effective on the 31st day after enactment', File 260770 §5(a), p. 56 of its 'Leg Final' attachment; File 260724, p. 10 of its attachment); counted from the Oct 13, 2026 enactment that is November 13, 2026, a legal date computed by Pier & Point and not printed in the text. Until then the adopted 100 ft limit applies. The enacted use rules were not checked for this record.

Floor area of Block 12, in detail: the project's MEP engineer (Meyers+) gives approximately 430,000 sq ft of office for Blocks 11 and 12 combined, with below-grade parking. The Oct 7, 2020 Phase 1 approval lists Block 12 at approximately 177,000 sq ft of commercial (plus 6,000 PDR, 25,000 entertainment, arts and recreation, and 27,000 accessory parking) and Block 11 at approximately 219,000 sq ft of commercial.
Bus shelter and restroom at Block 12: a 100% Schematic Design plan set incorporating SFMTA/Public Works feedback was sent to those agencies January 7, 2022.

open_questions: No design review approval or construction-start date found for Block 12; the most recent primary source found (the 2024 annual compliance report) describes design as 'under review', not approved.

The combined 430,000 sq ft figure for Blocks 11+12 comes from the project's MEP engineer (Meyers+). The Planning Department's October 7, 2020 Phase 1 approval lists approximately 177,000 sq ft of commercial space for Block 12 and 219,000 for Block 11 (about 396,000 together, plus PDR, retail and other uses); no source reconciles the two figures.

The Chronicle's July 2026 report of a proposed +23 ft height increase and added residential flexibility is tied to the Development Agreement and Planning Code amendment package (BOS Files 260724 and 260770), which passed the Board of Supervisors on first reading on Sept 29, 2026 and finally on Oct 6, 2026 (11 ayes), and Legistar lists it enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Legistar: Mayor 'APPROVED'; enactment numbers 208-26 and 209-26; page read Oct 14, 2026). The enacted height map labels Block 12 "123'" with a 115 ft limit for a majority non-residential building (File 260770 'Leg Final' attachment, p. 29), the 23 ft the Chronicle reported, effective November 13, 2026 by our count (a legal date computed by Pier & Point, not printed in the text). The enacted use rules (residential on Block 12) have not yet been checked against this record, so its use fact still shows the adopted rule.

Whether Blocks 11 and 12 are described as a life-science campus anywhere: the Meyers+ page, which pairs them, describes about 430,000 sq ft of office (its list of uses for the wider project includes laboratory), and the 2024 annual compliance report treats them together in a single 'Blocks 11 and 12 Design Review Application' without calling them a life-science campus; the D4D permits laboratory/life-science use on Block 12, and the Chronicle (July 29, 2026) quotes developer Enrique Landa saying all commercial parcels can be 'all PDR, all offices, all life sciences or all labs', but no cited source says that is the plan for Block 12.

Corrected 2026-10-06 (accuracy audit, October 2026): the July 2026 Development Agreement amendment request was shown as an expected event after it had been made and heard; it is now shown as having happened, with the Planning Commission's unanimous approval (SF Standard, August 3, 2026). Update 2026-10-12: the Board of Supervisors passed the amendment package on first reading on Sept 29, 2026 (see milestones). Update 2026-10-17: Legistar lists the package as approved by the Mayor and enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Enactment Nos. 208-26 and 209-26; page read Oct 17, 2026); the Board's final passage on Oct 6, 2026 (Ayes: 11) is shown by the Clerk of the Board's certificate in each file's 'Leg Final' attachment (File 260724 attachment pp. 11-12; File 260770 attachment pp. 58-59), although the Legistar web page's 10/6/2026 history row carries no action text.
